title: membrane_evo L7[L3]: the up-vs-twin sweep replicates on 4 fresh seeds; selection is carried by giant K2 cells surviving imposed disk deaths
summary: I re-ran the up, twin and down arms with the lab's evotrack ledger on fresh seeds 21-24 (down on 21) and labkit packs of up (seeds 21, 22) and twin (seed 21) to t=40000. K2 biomass share up vs identical-event twin: 0.93/0.78/0.82/0.65 vs 0.46/0.30/0.02/0.48 (4/4), K2 count share higher in 3/4; down purges K2 (0.00 vs 0.46). Conversions 0-1 per run (<= flips), first acquisitions 0-1, off-kind daughters 0. In the up arm K2 has fewer births than K1 on 4/4 seeds (4-20 vs 27-44) and almost no deaths (0-4 vs 25-38, mostly disk deaths): high-yield cells grow into giant irregular cells that the imposed r=14 disks cannot erase, so the sweep is by size and survival under imposed disturbance more than by births. The same seed's twin keeps K2 cells at normal size (rerun_twin/sheet.png vs rerun_up/seed21/sheet.png, t=24250-29500).

verdicts.limitation: Selection is disturbance-mediated: K2 wins mainly by growing into giant cells that survive the imposed r=14 death disks (K2 deaths 0-4 vs K1 25-38 per run) while having fewer births than K1, so this is selection through survival under an imposed death regime, not through intrinsic deaths. B not checked: I saw an L-link rim (rerun_up/seed21/radial.png, rim/core 1.47) but did not run the chi=0 ablation in this world. The claim names no track and I did not follow one individual through all capabilities, so the same-individuals condition is population-level only. Biomass share is dominated by a few giant cells; whole-cell flips of a large cell move it by tens of percent (rerun_up/seed21 t=31250-34500).
